statement: For contiguous float64 arrays, the stable crossover size for np.exp versus a Python loop using math.exp will be at least one power-of-two size bin smaller than the crossover for np.add versus the corresponding Python addition loop.
For positive int64 inputs, np.remainder will reach its stable crossover against an indexed Python modulo loop at a smaller array size than np.add reaches against an indexed Python addition loop.

For contiguous float64 addition, using np.add(a, b, out=y) with a reused output array will reduce the stable crossover size by at least one power-of-two size bin relative to evaluating y = a + b, against the same preallocated-output Python loop.

For contiguous float64 inputs, the unfused NumPy expression x*x + 2*x + 1 will have a stable crossover at least one power-of-two size bin larger than a single np.add operation, when each is compared with a Python loop computing the same result into a preallocated output array.

For elementwise multiplication on the tested Apple Silicon system, float16 arrays will have a stable NumPy-versus-Python-loop crossover at least two power-of-two size bins larger than float32 arrays of the same logical length.

For float64 addition, a stride-16 one-dimensional view will have a stable NumPy-versus-indexed-Python-loop crossover at least two power-of-two size bins larger than a contiguous array with the same logical element count.

For selecting between two precomputed float64 arrays, np.where(mask, a, b) will reach its stable crossover against a Python if/else loop at least one power-of-two size bin earlier with a deterministic 50% pseudorandom mask than with an all-true mask.

For arrays containing Python integers with dtype=object, np.add will fail to achieve a stable speed advantage over an equivalent list-comprehension addition at every tested power-of-two size from 1 through 131072.

On a 100-bit concatenated deceptive trap-5 benchmark with population 100 and 20,000 fitness evaluations, a mutation controller that raises the bit-mutation rate from 1/L to 4/L whenever normalized mean pairwise Hamming diversity falls below 0.15 will increase optimum-reaching success over 30 deterministic seeds by at least 20 percentage points for elitist (mu+mu) replacement, but by no more than 10 percentage points for full generational replacement.

For a 512-bit OneMax problem with population 256 and an equal budget of 100,000 evaluations, a vectorized generational GA will have at least twofold lower median wall-clock time than a one-offspring steady-state (mu+1) GA implemented with the same NumPy data structures, while the steady-state GA will attain a median final best fitness at least one bit higher across seeds 0 through 29.

On the 100-bit concatenated trap-5 benchmark with population 100 and 50,000 evaluations, batched steady-state replacement with batch size 16, where all parents are selected from the same pre-batch population snapshot, will reduce optimum-reaching success by at least 15 percentage points relative to serial batch-size-1 replacement, while reducing median wall-clock time by at least 40% across 30 deterministic seeds.

Across runs of fixed-parameter generational, (mu+1), and (mu+mu) GAs on 128-bit Royal Road and concatenated trap-8 benchmarks, normalized mean per-locus genotype entropy measured after 25% of a 40,000-evaluation budget will predict eventual failure with pooled AUROC of at least 0.75 and an AUROC at least 0.10 higher than that obtained from the population fitness coefficient of variation.

On a 100-bit concatenated trap-5 benchmark under a 50,000-evaluation budget, four islands of 25 individuals with ring migration of one elite every 10 generations will achieve an optimum-reaching success rate at least 15 percentage points higher than a panmictic population of 100, and will retain at least 25% greater normalized Hamming diversity at half-budget, across seeds 0 through 29.

For 40-bit Jump functions with jump sizes 4, 6, and 8, mutation that samples an exact number of flipped bits K with probability proportional to K^-1.5 will produce an aggregate optimum-reaching success rate at least 20 percentage points higher than standard independent bit mutation at rate 1/L within 100,000 evaluations, while requiring no more than 1.5 times the median evaluations of standard mutation on OneMax.

In a generational GA with population 100 and 40,000 evaluations on a 100-bit concatenated trap-5 problem, one-point crossover will exceed uniform crossover's optimum-reaching success rate by at least 20 percentage points when each five-bit trap block is contiguous, but by no more than 5 percentage points after a fixed random permutation disperses the bits of every block, across 30 deterministic seeds.

On 100-bit OneMax observed through additive Gaussian fitness noise with standard deviation 4, an elitist (mu+mu) GA that caches noisy scores will finish at least three true-fitness points below a non-elitist (mu,mu) GA after an equal budget of 50,000 noisy evaluations; replacing cached elite scores with the mean of three fresh evaluations, counted against the same budget, will remove at least half of that deficit across seeds 0 through 29.

On eight fixed 64-bit NK landscapes with K=6, population 80, a 15,000-evaluation budget, and seeds 0 through 9, a diversity-adaptive tournament controller that uses tournament size 2 when mean per-locus entropy is below 0.25, size 5 when it is above 0.40, and otherwise retains its current size will improve mean final normalized fitness by at least 0.5 percentage points over fixed size-5 tournaments for steady-state and (μ+μ) replacement, but by less than 0.2 percentage points for generational and steady-generational replacement.

On 100-bit moving-target OneMax, where eight target bits flip every 4,000 evaluations, a population-100 steady-state GA injecting one random immigrant every 20 evaluations will require at least 25% fewer median evaluations to recover 95 matching bits after each change than a generational GA replacing five population members with immigrants per 100-evaluation generation; on static OneMax, their median final best fitness after 40,000 evaluations will differ by no more than one bit across seeds 0 through 29.

For 10-dimensional continuous optimization with 2,000 true evaluations and seeds 0 through 19, a real-coded GA that refits a quadratic ridge-regression surrogate every 20 evaluations and uses it to select one of eight candidate offspring for true evaluation will achieve at least fivefold lower median final simple regret than a conventional GA on Sphere, while reducing median regret by no more than 20% on Rastrigin; both methods will use identical population, crossover, mutation, and true-evaluation budgets.

On ten deterministic 100-vertex balanced graph-bisection instances formed from two 50-vertex cliques plus 100 seeded cross-clique edges, a population-100 GA using balance-preserving swap mutation will reach the planted bisection in at least 20 percentage points more runs than an otherwise identical GA using independent bit mutation followed by random cardinality repair, within 30,000 evaluations and across seeds 0 through 19.

Across ten fixed 80-bit NK landscapes with K=6, population 100, 30,000 evaluations, and seeds 0 through 9, choosing the second parent as the most Hamming-distant of five tournament-selected candidates will increase midpoint population diversity by at least 20% and mean final normalized fitness by at least 0.4 percentage points relative to independent tournament mating; on 80-bit OneMax, the same mating rule will increase median evaluations needed to first reach fitness 79 by at least 15%.

On a 40-bit concatenated trap-4 phenotype represented redundantly by 80 genotype bits decoded as pairwise XOR, a population-100 (μ+μ) GA that permits at most two survivors per decoded phenotype will exceed the optimum-reaching success rate of a GA permitting at most two survivors per exact genotype by at least 20 percentage points within 40,000 evaluations across seeds 0 through 29; with direct 40-bit encoding, the two duplicate-control rules will differ by no more than 5 percentage points.

On a 64-bit Royal Road function with eight-bit blocks, population 64, one-point crossover, mutation rate 1/64, and seeds 0 through 29, a (μ+1) GA will generate at least 1.8 offspring attempts per cache-miss fitness evaluation, versus at most 1.2 for a generational GA; consequently, its median counted-evaluation advantage in reaching fitness 56 under cache-miss-only accounting will shrink by at least half when every attempted offspring, including cached duplicates, is charged to the 20,000-evaluation budget.

Across ten fixed 64-bit NK landscapes with K=4, population 100, 20,000 evaluations, and seeds 0 through 9, fitness-proportional selection using weights exp(10z), where z is objective fitness normalized to [0,1], will produce at least 25% lower mean per-locus entropy at quarter-budget and at least 0.5 percentage points lower mean final normalized fitness than proportional selection using weights 1+z; tournament selection with the same random streams will produce identical trajectories under the two monotonic transformations.

On a 40-bit weighted exact-cardinality problem requiring exactly 20 one-bits, with population 50, an initialization cap of 400 candidate draws, and seeds 0 through 49, rejection-based Bernoulli initialization will fail to create a full population in at least 35 percentage points more runs than constructive sampling without replacement; among runs that initialize successfully, the algorithms' mean final-best score and best-so-far AUC after 10,000 evaluations will each differ by less than 1%.

On an 80-bit weighted exact-cardinality problem requiring exactly 40 one-bits, with population 80 and 8,000 accepted-offspring evaluations per run, independent bit mutation at rate 1/80 followed by rejection and resampling will require at least 1.6 offspring attempts per accepted offspring and record misses on at least 35% of attempts, whereas a one-for-one swap mutation will require exactly one attempt and zero feasibility misses across seeds 0 through 29.

Across 30 fixed 64-bit NK landscapes with K=6, comparing tournament sizes 2 and 4 using identical initial populations and landscape seeds, the standard error of the paired per-seed difference in final normalized fitness will be at least 30% smaller than the median standard error obtained from 1,000 deterministic random permutations of the second algorithm's seed labels.

For population-60 generational and elitist (μ+μ) GAs on a 60-bit concatenated trap-5 benchmark, using 12,000 evaluations and seeds 0 through 49, the half-budget fraction of duplicate individuals in the current population will predict failure to reach the optimum with pooled AUROC at least 0.75 and at least 0.10 higher than the AUROC of the duplicate ratio among all offspring attempts up to half-budget.

Across 20 fixed 80-bit NK landscapes with K=6 and a 20,000-evaluation budget, tournament-size-5 selection will exceed tournament-size-2 selection by at least 0.5 percentage points in mean normalized best-so-far AUC over the first half of the budget, while tournament-size-2 selection will exceed tournament-size-5 selection by at least 0.3 percentage points in mean final normalized fitness.

On 60-bit OneMax with population 20, bit mutation rate 2/60, target fitness 56, 12,000 evaluations, and seeds 0 through 49, a non-elitist generational GA will have at least 20% of runs in which the target counter records one or more hits but the terminal-population best score is below 56; an otherwise matched elitist (μ+μ) GA will have zero such runs.

For target-stopped population-50 generational and steady-state GAs on 32-bit OneMax, with target 32, a maximum of 15,000 evaluations, and seeds 0 through 99, the unweighted mean of per-run generated-candidate duplicate ratios will differ by at least 10% relative from the ratio reconstructed by pooling duplicate counts and attempt denominators for at least one algorithm.

When generational and steady-state GAs are run for seeds 0 through 29 on 64-bit OneMax, deriving an independent random-number substream from each (algorithm, seed) pair will produce byte-identical per-seed records when algorithm execution order is reversed, whereas using one shared global pseudorandom stream will change at least 80% of rows in one or more of initialization attempts, offspring attempts, duplicate ratio, or either score.

For 30 deterministic synthetic Python experiments packaged as single RO-Crate-style ZIP archives containing source, a hash-locked transitive wheelhouse, an environment specification, UTC run provenance, and JSON outputs, a SHA-256 content identifier for each archive will resolve after relocation to three different filesystem roots, and every relocated archive will pass 100% of manifest-hash checks and reproduce its archived output byte-for-byte in a fresh virtual environment.

Across 20 synthetic experiments with two-level local dependency graphs, bundles that vendor every transitive dependency artifact with recorded SHA-256 hashes will reconstruct successfully offline in all 20 cases after the original package repository is deleted, whereas version-pinned manifests that omit transitive artifacts will fail reconstruction in at least 15 cases.

For 100 copies of a complete computational bundle, independently changing one byte in the source, one dependency artifact, the environment specification, or the machine-readable output will always change the bundle's SHA-256 persistent identifier and cause manifest verification to fail, while changing only the bundle's filesystem path will never change the identifier.

For 50 pairs of semantically identical RO-Crate metadata documents generated with randomized JSON key order, whitespace, and entity order, hashing raw ZIP bytes will assign different identifiers to at least 90% of pairs, whereas hashing a bundle representation using canonical JSON, normalized archive paths, fixed file permissions, and fixed ZIP timestamps will assign the same identifier to all 50 pairs.

When the same deterministic program is executed twice in clean environments from one archived bundle, including wall-clock timestamps inside the scientific output will prevent byte-identical output in all 30 paired reruns, whereas separating execution timestamps into provenance metadata and using a fixed logical run timestamp in the output will yield byte-identical output in all 30 pairs.

For a deterministic seeded genetic-algorithm run archived with its source, complete local dependency artifacts, interpreter and platform specification, seed, parameters, and JSON output, replay in two independently created virtual environments will reproduce the output byte-for-byte for all 20 seeds; deleting any one of the seed, dependency hashes, or interpreter-version constraints will cause at least one of three deliberately compatible-looking alternative reconstructions to produce a different output or become unverifiable.

Across 20 bundles whose metadata references source, environment, and outputs by external relative or file URIs, moving the metadata document without its original directory tree will leave fewer than 25% of component references resolvable, while packaging the same components inside one archive with identifier-relative paths and per-entity hashes will leave 100% resolvable after the archive is moved and renamed.

For 30 deterministic Python zipapp executables built from identical archived source and dependencies, ordinary builds that preserve current file timestamps will produce at least 25 distinct executable hashes, whereas builds using sorted archive entries, normalized permissions, and a fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH will produce one executable hash; archiving that executable hash in the unified research object will detect every deliberately substituted noncanonical build.

On the 80-bit concatenated trap-4 benchmark, a calibration using seeds 0-39 will choose population size from {32, 64, 96}, mutation rate from {1/80, 2/80, 4/80}, and budget from {8000, 16000, 32000} by minimizing the absolute distance of serial success from 0.50, with deterministic tie-breaking. On 128 preregistered paired seeds starting at 1000, a serial elitist steady-state GA will exceed an otherwise identical frozen-parent batch-size-16 GA by at least 10 percentage points in optimum-reaching success, and the lower endpoint of a 95% paired Newcombe confidence interval for serial minus batch success will be above zero.

On 80-bit OneMax with target fitness 80, parameters independently calibrated by the same prespecified grid-and-tie-breaking procedure to give serial success between 0.35 and 0.65, the absolute paired success-rate difference between serial elitist steady-state replacement and frozen-parent batch-size-16 replacement will be no greater than 5 percentage points across 192 held-out seed pairs, with the 95% paired confidence interval contained within the equivalence bounds [-0.10, 0.10].

In the independently calibrated 80-bit trap-4 regime, optimum-reaching success across 128 held-out paired seeds will show a batch-size dose response: frozen-parent batch size 16 will be at least 8 percentage points less successful than batch size 4, while batch size 4 will be no more than 5 percentage points less successful than serial batch size 1; all variants will use the same initial populations, operators, and total evaluation budget.

Across 40 deterministic calibration-validation splits constructed from a precomputed 400-seed outcome table for the trap-4 parameter grid, using 64 calibration seeds rather than 16 will increase by at least 20 percentage points the fraction of selected regimes whose serial success on a disjoint 64-seed validation block lies in the prespecified informative interval [0.30, 0.70].

Across the same 40 deterministic calibration-validation splits, the median absolute deviation of serial success from the calibration target 0.50 will be at least 0.08 larger on held-out validation seeds than on the seeds used to select population size, mutation rate, and budget; reusing the selection seeds as confirmatory observations will therefore overstate calibration accuracy.

Using a reservoir of 512 held-out paired serial and batch-size-16 outcomes from the calibrated trap-4 regime, deterministic resampling will show that increasing the preregistered sample size from 30 pairs, as used in the earlier comparison, to 128 pairs reduces the median width of the 95% paired success-difference confidence interval by at least 40% and reduces the fraction of intervals spanning both -0.10 and 0.10 by at least 30 percentage points.

For the calibrated trap-4 population size and mutation rate, the selected budget B will produce at least 1.5 times as many serial-versus-batch discordant success pairs as either the floor regime B/4 or the saturated regime 4B across 128 matched seeds, and the paired confidence interval for the success difference at B will be at least 25% narrower than at each alternative budget.

In the calibrated trap-4 comparison, changing only the batch-budget boundary rule among (i) evaluating a partial final batch, (ii) stopping before any incomplete final batch, and (iii) allowing one complete final batch to overshoot the nominal budget by at most 15 evaluations will change batch-size-16 success by no more than 2 percentage points across 256 held-out seeds, with each 95% paired confidence interval contained within [-0.05, 0.05].

In the population-100, 100-bit concatenated trap-5 comparison, using the same fixed selection, crossover, mutation, and replacement settings as the earlier 50,000-evaluation experiment, 96 fresh deterministic seed pairs with shared initial populations and identical evaluation-indexed operator schedules will show an absolute serial-versus-frozen-parent-batch-size-16 optimum-reaching success-rate difference of no more than 5 percentage points at 100,000 evaluations.

Under the same paired trap-5 protocol and 96 held-out seed pairs, serial elitist steady-state replacement will exceed frozen-parent batch-size-16 replacement in optimum-reaching success by at least 8 percentage points at the prospectively specified 250,000-evaluation checkpoint.

Under the same paired trap-5 protocol and 96 held-out seed pairs, serial elitist steady-state replacement will exceed frozen-parent batch-size-16 replacement in optimum-reaching success by at least 12 percentage points at the prospectively specified 500,000-evaluation checkpoint, with more serial-only than batch-only discordant pairs.

Among paired runs in which neither algorithm has reached the trap-5 optimum by 100,000 evaluations, frozen-parent batch-size-16 populations will have at least 10% greater mean normalized per-locus genotype entropy than their matched serial populations at that checkpoint.

Among paired runs in which neither algorithm has reached the optimum by 100,000 evaluations, serial populations will contain an average of at least one more fully solved all-ones trap-5 block in their best individual than matched frozen-parent batch-size-16 populations.

For algorithm-runs that have not succeeded by 100,000 evaluations, the number of fully solved trap-5 blocks in the best individual at 100,000 evaluations will predict success by 500,000 evaluations with leave-one-seed-pair-out AUROC of at least 0.75 and an AUROC at least 0.10 higher than normalized per-locus genotype entropy.

After deterministically dividing the 96 shared initial populations into tertiles by initial best fitness, the serial-minus-batch-size-16 success-rate difference at 500,000 evaluations will be at least 10 percentage points larger in the lowest-initial-fitness tertile than in the highest-initial-fitness tertile.

Across all 96 paired runs, defining time to success as the first optimum evaluation and censoring failures at 500,000 evaluations, serial elitist steady-state replacement will have a paired mean restricted time to success at least 40,000 evaluations lower than frozen-parent batch-size-16 replacement.

Across 24 clean checkouts placed in filesystem roots that vary in depth and include spaces and non-ASCII characters, the documented one-command procedure will complete successfully in every checkout and regenerate exactly four CSV files and one heatmap source matrix byte-for-byte identical to the released references, with every generated file passing its manifest checksum and validation rule.

For all 18 combinations of three PYTHONHASHSEED values, three supported locale settings, and two time zones, execution of the package's one-command reproduction procedure in fresh locked environments will produce identical SHA-256 hashes for all four CSV files and the heatmap source matrix.

A schema-aware manifest validator will reject at least 57 of 60 deterministically generated structurally invalid package variants—covering missing files, renamed files, duplicate logical roles, undeclared files, incorrect media types, and unsupported schema identifiers—while accepting all 20 independently repacked valid variants.

For 20 valid version-1 manifests with randomized field and entity order, deterministic migration to manifest schema version 2 will preserve the resolved input, output, command, and checksum sets in all cases and produce one canonical version-2 representation, whereas each of 20 manifests declaring an unsupported major schema version will fail before source-code execution begins.

Across 12 synthetic local package repositories in which a transitive dependency has both an original version and a newer API-incompatible version, installation from the hash-locked environment file will reproduce the reference outputs in all 12 cases, while installation from direct dependencies with permissive version ranges will either fail or change at least one of the five output hashes in at least 10 cases.

For 40 fault-injected package copies spanning missing source modules, absent CSV inputs, absent heatmap matrices, malformed manifests, and unsatisfied lock entries, the one-command procedure will terminate nonzero before analysis execution in at least 38 cases, emit the correct stage-specific diagnostic code in at least 36 cases, and leave all previously validated reference outputs unchanged in every case.

Among 40 coordinated output mutations whose altered files have valid formats and freshly recomputed manifest checksums, relational validation rules linking seed identifiers, row counts, summary values, and heatmap cells across the four CSV files and matrix will detect at least 36 mutations, while all 20 unmodified regenerated output sets will pass.

Across 30 deterministic failures injected at different points while regenerating the four CSV files and heatmap matrix, an atomic staging-and-publish implementation will leave the output directory in either the complete old state or the complete new state in all 30 trials, whereas an otherwise identical in-place implementation will leave a mixed or incomplete output set in at least 21 trials.

In five fresh checkouts executed in the same immutable container image with all network interfaces disabled before invocation, the literal command `make reproduce` will exit 0 every time and generate all four CSV files and the heatmap source matrix with SHA-256 hashes identical to the released references.

When the checkout is mounted read-only except for the manifest-declared output directory and a fresh temporary directory, `make reproduce` will exit 0 in all five trials, reproduce the five reference hashes, and produce no attempted writes to source files, user-home paths, or other filesystem locations.

Across four paired clean-container trials with `MAKEFLAGS=-j1` and `MAKEFLAGS=-j8`, while invoking the same literal command `make reproduce`, every run will exit 0 and the complete generated-file inventory and SHA-256 hashes will be identical between serial and parallel make execution.

If executable decoys named `python`, `python3`, and `pip` that log their use and exit 97 are prepended to `PATH`, three fresh executions of `make reproduce` will still exit 0, invoke none of the decoys, and report an interpreter path inside the recorded container environment while reproducing all five reference hashes.

For each of five trials in which all declared output files are prepopulated with syntactically valid stale content and timestamps set 24 hours in the future, `make reproduce` will regenerate every declared output rather than treating it as up to date, exit 0, and restore all five released reference hashes.

When exactly one released reference output is replaced by a format-valid but content-altered counterpart in each of five isolated trials, `make reproduce` will regenerate the normal outputs but return a nonzero exit status in all five trials, identify the mismatching logical output on stderr, and never report overall reproduction success.

Across six independent clean-container runs of `make reproduce`, a provenance capture harness will produce records containing the checkout revision, immutable image identifier, resolved interpreter path, literal command, integer exit status, separately hashed stdout and stderr logs, generated-file inventory, generated hashes, reference hashes, and per-output comparison results; an independent verifier will recompute and confirm every recorded field in all six records.

In three paired trials under a 512 MiB memory limit with one CPU and under a 2 GiB limit with two CPUs, the literal command `make reproduce` will exit 0 in every trial and produce identical hashes for all five deliverables, with no out-of-memory termination, timeout, or resource-dependent output mismatch.

Across 40 deterministically altered release archives spanning source, schema, lock file, Makefile, README, outputs, raw results, logs, mutation specifications, and figure, an adversary that changes one target and recomputes every internal inventory and SHA-256 entry will cause an internal-only verifier to accept all 40 archives, whereas comparison with a separately published original archive SHA-256 digest will reject all 40.

For 24 deterministic TAR variants that preserve every regular-file byte sequence but alter executable mode bits, convert symbolic links into regular files containing the same target text, or change archive entry types, a path-and-SHA-256-only verifier will accept all 24, while an enriched inventory recording path, entity type, link target, and normalized permission mode will reject all 24 and accept all 12 unmodified controls.

A pre-extraction archive verifier that rejects absolute paths, parent-directory traversal, duplicate normalized paths, backslash aliases, Unicode-normalization collisions, and case-fold collisions will reject all 36 deterministically constructed ambiguous or unsafe ZIP archives while accepting all 12 portable controls; a verifier that checks only raw entry names and matching SHA-256 values will accept all 36 unsafe archives.

For 32 deterministically salted bundles, a builder that attempts to include the SHA-256 of its checksum table inside that same table will fail to reach a byte-identical fixed point within 100 rebuild iterations in every case, whereas a two-layer design that excludes the table from its own entries and covers it with a detached archive digest will produce an identical table and archive digest on two successive deterministic builds in all 32 cases.

For 20 synthetic Git repositories containing LF-normalized tracked text files, constructing a release from a fresh checkout configured with `core.autocrlf=true` will retain the same HEAD commit identifier but change at least one tracked-file SHA-256 value in all 20 repositories, while constructing the source portion with `git archive HEAD` will match the committed blob bytes for every tracked file in all 20.

Across 16 synthetic superprojects containing both a local Git submodule and a Git-LFS-style pointer whose object identifier names a local content blob, verification of the top-level commit will succeed for every payload that omits the materialized submodule tree and large-file content, while a closure-aware inventory will reject all 16 incomplete payloads and accept all 16 counterparts containing and hashing the referenced contents.

For 48 deterministic metadata mutations that preserve every payload file and SHA-256 value but delete, redirect, or swap provenance links among commands, source, raw results, logs, outputs, mutation specifications, and figure, a role-aware provenance-closure validator will reject at least 46 mutations while accepting all 16 unmodified release graphs.

On 20 valid synthetic releases containing every committed file plus explicitly declared generated outputs and exclusions, and 40 invalid releases containing either an omitted committed file, an undeclared extra file, or a tracked file falsely reclassified as generated, a role-aware repository-to-release reconciliation algorithm will classify all 60 correctly; strict commit/release set equality will reject all 20 valid releases, and a simple rule requiring only that committed paths be a subset of release paths will accept all 20 invalid variants containing undeclared extras.

Across four executions in fresh locked environments with the output directory initially absent, syscall tracing will show that each of the three target CSV paths is created after execution begins, is written before any read of that path, and produces its assigned stated SHA-256 digest in every run.

Across 12 clean package copies in which every declared input retains identical bytes but input modification times are deterministically varied from 1980 through 2038 and readable permission modes alternate between 0444 and 0644, all three regenerated CSV files will retain their assigned stated SHA-256 digests.

For ten replicas of the declared input tree constructed with identical paths and bytes but ten deterministic file-creation orders, including lexical, reverse-lexical, and eight seeded permutations, the independently executed package will regenerate the same three stated SHA-256 digests in every replica.

In eight fresh locked-environment runs spanning internal numerical-library thread limits of one, two, four, and eight via OMP_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, and NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS, all three CSV files will reproduce their assigned stated SHA-256 digests exactly.

Three paired executions from byte-identical source snapshots—one normal Git checkout, one snapshot with the .git directory removed, and one snapshot produced by git archive—will all complete successfully and regenerate the three assigned stated SHA-256 digests.

Across four fresh executions with PYTHONPATH pointing to a hostile directory containing sitecustomize.py and usercustomize.py files that write marker files and terminate with exit code 93 if imported, the package will import neither decoy, exit successfully, and regenerate all three stated SHA-256 digests.

In six locked-environment executions covering numeric user IDs 1000 and 2000 crossed with umasks 0022, 0027, and 0077, each run will regenerate all three CSV files with the assigned stated SHA-256 digests, although their ownership or permission metadata may differ.

For each of three independently regenerated CSV files, Python hashlib, GNU sha256sum, OpenSSL dgst, and a separately implemented pure-Python SHA-256 routine will compute the same digest, and that unanimous digest will equal the file's preassigned stated value; additionally, all five nonidentity permutations of the filename-to-digest mapping will fail at least two comparisons.

Across 20 paired fresh workspaces instantiated from the same locked ISO root filesystem, an independently implemented POSIX-shell runner and Python-standard-library runner consuming the same machine-readable protocol will agree on every preflight field and warning code, return the same exit status, and produce identical generated-file inventories and SHA-256 digests matching all released references in every pair.

For 16 deterministic permutations of the preflight-check order executed by each of two independent runners in fresh ISO-derived workspaces, the normalized set of preflight results, warnings, and failure codes will be identical across runners and permutations, no declared output will be created during preflight, and every passing permutation will produce the same reference artifact hashes.

In 12 paired executions, one runner using an empty HOME and XDG configuration tree and another using a deterministically populated tree containing conflicting Git, pip, Matplotlib, and generic application configuration files will obtain identical preflight records and reference artifact hashes; filesystem tracing will show that none of the hostile configuration files influenced execution.

Across 10 paired fresh-system trials, an interactive runner attached to a pseudo-terminal and a headless runner with stdin closed and stdout and stderr redirected will both complete without prompts or input reads, report identical preflight outcomes, and generate identical reference artifact hashes.

In eight trials where two independent runners start simultaneously in separate fresh workspaces but share the same host temporary directory, both runners will exit successfully, produce identical reference artifact hashes, and show no reads, writes, renames, or deletions of paths created by the other runner.

For 32 deterministic single-fault package variants spanning missing tools, unreadable inputs, malformed lock data, insufficient free-space declarations, unsupported interpreter versions, and unwritable output locations, two independently implemented runners will agree on pass versus fail for all 32 variants, emit the same normalized preflight failure code for at least 30, and invoke no analysis command in every preflight-failing case.

Across 24 deterministic synthetic packages whose prose instructions ambiguously specify either the working directory, relative input root, or output destination, two fixed and reasonable runner interpretations will disagree on preflight or artifact outcome in at least 18 cases; after replacing each ambiguous instruction with an equivalent canonical machine-readable command and absolute role mapping, the same runners will agree on all 24 outcomes and artifact hashes.

For 20 seeded notebook-like bundles executed by two independent runners, every declared deterministic data artifact will be bitwise identical, while runner-specific metadata will make at least 15 of 20 rendered-output pairs hash-unequal; nevertheless, two independently implemented preregistered semantic comparators will assign every such pair a similarity score of at least 0.99 and will differ from each other by no more than 0.01, while rejecting all 20 counterparts containing a seeded substantive numerical or graphical mutation with scores below 0.95.

On a runner where `docker info`, `docker version`, and `docker ps` all exit 0 immediately before testing, each of six primary executions and its six seed-matched replay executions will exit 0 within 1,200 seconds, yielding a strict completion count of 12/12 and no maximum elapsed time above 1,000 seconds.

For all six seed-matched primary-replay pairs that terminate successfully, replay elapsed time will not exceed its corresponding primary elapsed time by more than 10%, and the median replay elapsed time will be at least 5% lower than the median primary elapsed time.

When the six replay executions use newly created workspaces, anonymous volumes, container names, and temporary directories rather than retaining primary-run state, their exit-status and under-1,200-second classifications will match those of six state-retaining replays in every seed-matched case, with median elapsed times differing by no more than 15%.

After all required images are locally available, restarting the Docker daemon between the six primary and six replay executions will not change any replay terminal status or image digest, and every replay will still exit 0 within 1,200 seconds with daemon-restart recovery adding less than 30 seconds to any measured execution.

Across the twelve primary and replay executions, host-side `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` timing and elapsed time reconstructed from Docker event timestamps will differ by no more than one second per execution and will assign identical before-versus-after-1,200-second classifications in all twelve cases.

In twelve deterministic boundary tests using a dependency-injected monotonic clock—four each ending at 1,199.999, 1,200.000, and 1,200.001 seconds—the timing harness will classify all 1,199.999-second executions as within the timed section and all 1,200.000- and 1,200.001-second executions as outside it, while preserving the underlying process exit status separately.

For twelve synthetic Docker workflows comprising three successful controls and nine runtime-failure cases—invalid entrypoint, missing bind-mount input, read-only output, memory-limit termination, nonzero application exit, killed daemon connection, unavailable local image, exhausted quota-backed output volume, and an internal timeout—all three Docker diagnostics will pass before every case, while the execution harness will correctly classify all nine failures and accept only the three controls.

For six paired synthetic container fixtures in which the container's designated parent process exits 0 but a descendant either continues computing or keeps a declared output open, a naive parent-exit monitor will report all six as completed, whereas a process-tree-aware monitor will reject all six until every descendant has terminated and all declared outputs are closed; both monitors will accept six matched clean controls.

Across eight deterministic repositories crossed by SHA-1 versus SHA-256 object format and loose versus delta-packed storage, a repository verifier that reads the object database directly will produce exactly the same byte-preserving path, object-ID, object-type, and mode inventory as `git ls-tree -rz --full-tree` for every entry, including regular files, executable files, symbolic links, nested trees, and gitlinks.

For twelve repositories in which an authenticated commit object is assigned a replacement commit through `refs/replace` and the index, working tree, and sparse-checkout configuration describe different states, a raw-object verifier pinned to the authenticated object ID will return the original commit's tree inventory in all twelve cases, while ordinary replacement-aware Git traversal will return the adversarial replacement inventory in all twelve.

Across twenty deterministic references comprising lightweight tags, one-level and two-level annotated tags ending at commits, annotated tags ending at trees or blobs, and references retargeted after initial resolution, the verifier will agree with Git's commit-peeling result for every reference, reject every non-commit terminal object, and retain the initially pinned commit inventory after every subsequent reference retargeting.

For a synthetic repository containing at least forty legal Git pathnames with tabs, newlines, leading dashes, trailing spaces, decomposed Unicode, and non-UTF-8 bytes, a byte-oriented verifier will enumerate every pathname exactly once and round-trip every original name through its encoded inventory, whereas a line-delimited UTF-8 replacement-decoding implementation will merge, split, or alter at least eight entries.

A strict object-graph verifier will accept all twelve canonical control repositories and reject all thirty raw-object fixtures containing exactly one of the following defects: truncated tree entries, zero or unavailable referenced object IDs, duplicate names, noncanonical ordering, illegal pathname bytes, unsupported modes, or mode-to-object-type mismatches; each rejection will occur before any working-tree materialization.

For eighteen commits containing dangling, absolute, parent-traversing, self-referential, and mutually cyclic symbolic-link targets, changing whether those targets exist on the host and changing their host-side contents will not alter any verifier output: every entry will remain mode 120000 with the exact committed blob bytes recorded as its target, while a comparator that follows links will fail or produce different content hashes in at least twelve cases.

Across twenty-four superproject commits containing eight consistent submodule configurations and sixteen cases with a missing `.gitmodules` entry, duplicate declared path, declaration for a non-gitlink path, or gitlink path absent from the declarations, the low-level verifier will identify every mode-160000 entry and its exact referenced commit ID without network access, while a separate materialization-readiness check will accept all eight consistent cases and flag all sixteen metadata inconsistencies.

In forty-eight tracked paths governed by deterministic root and nested `.gitattributes` rules, a commit-scoped attribute resolver will agree with Git on the effective `filter` attribute for all paths; the LFS verifier will accept all sixteen LFS-managed canonical pointer blobs whose local payload matches both declared SHA-256 OID and size, reject all sixteen LFS-managed malformed or payload-mismatched pointers, and classify all sixteen pointer-looking but non-LFS-managed blobs as ordinary authenticated Git blobs.

An exhaustive scan of all Unicode scalar values will find no non-ASCII scalar whose NFC form introduces U+002E FULL STOP, U+002F SOLIDUS, or U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS when that character was absent from the input, whereas NFKC will have at least five such scalars; consequently, in a 60-path corpus built from those scalars, NFKC-before-tokenization will create at least one new dot component, separator, or rooted path while NFC-before-tokenization will create none.

On 160 deterministic name pairs derived from Unicode CaseFolding.txt, the comparison key NFC(full_casefold(NFC(component))) applied component-wise will identify every pair labeled equivalent by Unicode full case folding, while NFC plus locale-independent lowercase will miss at least 20 pairs and ASCII-only folding will miss at least 40; all three methods will keep every one of 80 seeded non-equivalent controls distinct.

For 96 synthetic path components covering mixed-case device names, extensions on device names, trailing dots or spaces, COM1-COM9 and LPT1-LPT9 forms, superscript-digit COM/LPT forms, drive prefixes, UNC prefixes, and alternate-data-stream colons, a Win32 portability profile that applies trailing-dot/space trimming before reserved-basename testing and rejects namespace syntax will classify all 96 according to two independent implementations of the published Win32 naming rules, whereas the common regex ^(CON|PRN|AUX|NUL|COM[1-9]|LPT[1-9])$ applied to the raw component will misclassify at least 24.

A component trie that rejects canonical-path prefix conflicts will reject all 72 archives containing a regular file or symbolic link at canonical path p together with an entry below p, a file-directory type conflict at p, or two differently spelled implicit directories mapping to p, regardless of entry order; an exact-key-only duplicate detector will accept at least 48 of these archives, while both validators will accept all 24 nonconflicting controls.

Across 72 adversarial archives—36 ZIP files with conflicting local-header, central-directory, UTF-8-flag, and Unicode-path-extra-field names, and 36 TAR files with conflicting header, PAX path, and GNU long-name values—a policy that rejects any disagreement among applicable name sources will reject all 72 before extraction, while three independently selected archive parsers will disagree on the reported member name or destination for at least 24; all parsers and the policy will agree on all 24 unambiguous controls.

For a corpus containing every code point that was unassigned in Unicode 12.1 but has a canonical decomposition or nontrivial case-fold mapping in Unicode 15.1, canonical keys computed with the two versions will differ for at least 20 names; two implementations pinned to the same bundled Unicode 15.1 tables will agree on every key, whereas implementations using their runtime's unrecorded Unicode tables will disagree on at least those 20 when run against the two table versions.

A canonical encoding policy that accepts ASCII ZIP names without an encoding flag, requires valid shortest-form UTF-8 for every non-ASCII effective ZIP or TAR name, and rejects surrogate, overlong, truncated, and legacy-encoding ambiguity will accept all 80 multilingual UTF-8 controls and reject all 80 adversarial byte-name fixtures; a replacement-decoding validator will map at least 20 distinct adversarial names to the same comparison key or to the same key as a control.

For 40 archives each containing two or more faults drawn from malformed encoding, absolute or rooted syntax, dot components, Unicode or case-fold collisions, Windows aliases, exact duplicates, and prefix conflicts, a verifier that first parses all entries and then applies a documented fixed validation precedence to a canonical sorted inventory will emit the same primary rejection code for all 20 deterministic entry-order permutations of each archive; a streaming first-error verifier will emit different primary codes or construct different partial destination inventories for at least 25 of the 40 archives.

Let Δ_orig be the original 120-split mean paired performance difference between the originally favored optimization procedure and its comparator, with positive values favoring the original winner. On the access-controlled replication set, the frozen protocol will pass its preregistered regime check, produce sign(Δ_rep) = sign(Δ_orig), yield |Δ_rep| at least 0.50|Δ_orig|, and return a prespecified dependence-aware 95% bootstrap interval for Δ_rep that excludes zero in the original direction.

Across the complete preregistered robustness set, at least 90% of the paired-effect estimates will have the original direction, the minimum estimate will remain above zero, and the separately defined robustness interval will exclude zero; additionally, none of the prespecified secondary analyses will significantly favor the comparator after Holm correction at family-wise alpha 0.05.

Two independent implementations written from the time-stamped protocol, given the same replication data and deterministic seed manifest, will produce identical membership for all 120 splits, identical evaluated grid points, identical selected configurations including every tie, identical split-level scores, primary estimates agreeing within 1e-12, and identical bootstrap and robustness-interval endpoints.

In 200 deterministic null simulations matching the replication sample size and 120-split dependence structure, a protocol selected before outcome reveal will declare a positive optimization advantage in no more than 7% of simulations, whereas choosing after reveal among 20 plausible variants of the split seed, grid boundary, tie rule, bootstrap construction, or secondary-analysis subset will declare an advantage in at least 20%.

For 60 deterministic tie-rich synthetic datasets evaluated under 25 permutations of the same fixed grid, the preregistered total-order tie-breaking rule will select the same configuration and produce the same final 120-split estimate under every permutation; a first-encountered-maximum rule will select different configurations on at least 40 datasets and change the reported optimization winner on at least 15.

Across 150 deterministic no-signal synthetic datasets with 12 equally predictive candidate configurations and 120 outer splits, flat reuse of split outcomes for both grid selection and performance estimation will produce a nominal 95% interval excluding zero in favor of the selected procedure in at least 15% of datasets, while the preregistered nested procedure will do so in no more than 8%; the flat estimate's mean optimism relative to nested evaluation will be at least 0.01 on a unit-scale score.

In 200 deterministic simulations reproducing the overlap of observations across 120 splits, a naive bootstrap that resamples split-level estimates as independent units will have no more than 88% coverage for a nominal 95% interval, whereas the preregistered observation-level multiplier or cluster bootstrap will achieve 92% to 98% coverage and have median interval width at least 10% greater than the naive interval.

On 100 deterministic synthetic datasets satisfying the exact assumptions encoded by the preregistered regime check and 100 matched datasets each violating one encoded assumption, the frozen check will accept at least 95 satisfying datasets and reject at least 95 violating datasets; on the violating datasets, proceeding despite failure will reduce the primary interval's empirical coverage below 85%, compared with coverage between 92% and 98% on accepted datasets.

Across five bundled scikit-learn classification datasets, 30 deterministic stratified train-validation-test splits per dataset, and a fixed 24-candidate grid spanning linear, kernel, tree, and neighbor families, reversing candidate encounter order after rounding validation balanced accuracy to three decimals will change the selected internal identifier on at least 20% of splits and the selected family on at least 5%, but will change held-out balanced accuracy by at least 0.02 on fewer than one-third of the family-changing splits.

In 100 deterministic synthetic classification tasks whose candidate grids contain four differently labeled but parameter-identical aliases of each of six fitted configurations, forward versus reverse first-encountered tie-breaking will change the selected identifier on at least 95 tasks, while canonical hyperparameters, held-out predictions, and held-out scores will remain identical within 1e-12 on all 100.

Across 120 deterministic split-level selections on four small public datasets, reducing recorded validation-score precision from four decimal places to two will increase the forward-versus-reverse identifier-change frequency by at least a factor of three and the family-change frequency by at least a factor of two; it will also increase the frequency of absolute held-out score differences above 0.01 by at least five percentage points.

Using the same probabilistic predictions from 20 fixed classifiers on 150 deterministic validation splits, selection by validation accuracy will produce at least four times as many first-encountered ties and at least twice as many family changes under reversed order as selection by unrounded validation log loss; among accuracy-tied family switches, at least 15% will yield an absolute held-out log-loss difference above 0.02.

For 40 deterministic tie fixtures in which one family contributes eight validation-tied configuration identifiers and a second family contributes one, 1,000 seeded uniform random candidate orders per fixture will select the eight-identifier family in 85% to 92% of orders; after collapsing semantically identical configurations and sampling tied families uniformly, its selection frequency will fall to 47% to 53%.

Across 150 deterministic selections on five small public datasets, replacing exact three-decimal ties with a preregistered tolerance tie defined as scores within 0.005 of the recorded maximum will at least double the frequency with which reversed encounter order selects different families, yet no more than 15% of those tolerance-induced family switches will produce an absolute held-out balanced-accuracy difference above 0.02.

Among at least 100 validation-tied candidate pairs collected from deterministic repeated splits of four public datasets, the median absolute held-out score difference for cross-family pairs will be at least twice that for nonalias within-family pairs, while parameter-identical alias pairs will have a maximum held-out difference below 1e-12.

Across all family-spanning validation ties found in 150 deterministic splits of five small public classification datasets, an equal-weight soft-voting ensemble containing one canonical representative from every tied family will reduce mean held-out log-loss regret relative to the oracle-best tied candidate by at least 25% compared with first-encountered selection, and will match or beat both the forward-order and reverse-order selections on at least 55% of tie events.

Across 120 independent datasets at each of n=250 and n=2000 from a fixed 10-dimensional Gaussian-logistic classification DGP, using the same 12 nonalias candidate configurations and blocked five-fold balanced-accuracy validation, increasing n from 250 to 2000 will reduce the probability of an exact top-score tie by at least 50%, while changing the probability of a practical tie within 0.005 of the maximum by no more than 15 percentage points.

On 150 independent n=600 samples from one prespecified Gaussian-logistic DGP, replacing one blocked five-fold validation run with the mean of five prespecified blocked five-fold runs will reduce exact top-score tie incidence among a fixed 12-candidate grid by at least 30%, but the practical-tie incidence within 0.005 will differ by no more than 10 percentage points and the median Jaccard similarity of the two practical-tie sets will be at least 0.75.

Across 100 independent n=800 datasets tuned over 12 small random-forest and extremely-randomized-tree configurations, two independently seeded repetitions of blocked validation that use common folds and matched learner seeds across candidates will have a mean practical-tie-set Jaccard similarity at least 0.15 higher and a top-candidate agreement rate at least 10 percentage points higher than repetitions giving every candidate independent folds and learner seeds.

For 500 independent n=300 samples from a prespecified asymmetric one-dimensional logistic DGP, tuning 11 fixed probability-threshold classifiers whose population accuracies are all distinct by deterministic quadrature will nevertheless produce an exact validation-accuracy tie for the empirical optimum in at least 15% of samples; at least 80% of those tie events will contain candidates whose population accuracies differ by more than 0.001.

Across 12 preregistered Gaussian-logistic DGP regimes varying only intercept and signal strength, with 100 independent n=400 datasets per regime and the same 11-threshold candidate grid, the Spearman correlation between the deterministically computed population top-two accuracy gap and the observed frequency of practical validation ties within 0.005 will be at most -0.80; regimes with a population gap below 0.003 will have at least twice the tie incidence of regimes with a gap above 0.010.

Across 120 independent n=600 datasets from a fixed nonlinear binary-classification DGP, replacing a nested 12-candidate coarse grid with a 36-candidate dense grid containing no prediction-identical aliases will at least double the median size of the 0.005 practical-tie set, while at least 80% of newly admitted tied candidates will belong to the same model family as a coarse-grid minimizer and the cross-family tie-event rate will change by no more than 10 percentage points.

Among all candidate pairs falling within 0.005 of the best blocked-validation balanced accuracy across 150 independent n=500 datasets from a fixed Gaussian-mixture classification DGP, evaluation on two independent n=1000 test samples will reverse the pairwise performance ordering for at least 25% of pairs, and at least 20% of validation tie events will contain no candidate that ranks first on both test samples.

Across 150 independent n=600 datasets from a prespecified nonlinear classification DGP and a fixed 16-candidate cross-family grid, retaining every candidate within 0.005 of the best blocked-validation balanced accuracy will include the independently determined best-generalizing fitted candidate at least 20 percentage points more often than retaining only the validation winner, while the practical-tie set will have median size no greater than four.

Across 48 deterministic outer splits from the synthetic DGP X~N(0,1), P(Y=1|X)=sigmoid(X), with base predictions q=signal(1.8X+0.6), selecting an affine-logit calibrator sigmoid(a*logit(q)+b) from a locked 11-by-11 grid using mean 15-bin ECE over exactly 16 calibration seeds of n=250 each will yield an independently evaluated mean paired ECE reduction of at least 0.08, and at least 60% of split-level reductions will individually reach 0.08.

On the same 48-split affine-logit calibration benchmark, expanding a nested locked grid from 25 to 121 candidates by densifying the same parameter bounds will increase the independently evaluated mean paired ECE reduction by no more than 0.01 while changing the selected parameter pair on at least 40% of splits.

Across 48 deterministic splits from P(Y=1|X)=sigmoid(X) with more severely distorted base predictions q=sigmoid(3X+1.2), a locked 121-candidate grid that widens the affine-logit parameter range to include the population-optimal inverse transformation will produce an independently evaluated mean paired ECE reduction at least 0.03 larger than an equally sized 121-candidate grid that only densifies the original narrow range.

Across 60 deterministic splits using 16 calibration seeds of n=75 and a locked 21-by-21 affine-logit grid, estimating the paired ECE reduction on the same seeded samples used for selection will exceed the reduction on independent matched samples by at least 0.015 on average, and at least 20% of splits will cross 0.08 only under the reused-sample estimate.

For each of 60 deterministic splits evaluated over a locked 121-candidate affine-logit grid, selections made separately from the odd-numbered and even-numbered halves of the same 16-seed manifest will choose the identical parameter pair on no more than 50% of splits, yet their independently evaluated paired ECE reductions will differ by a median of no more than 0.01.

Across 30 deterministic outer splits and 10 repeated 16-seed selection manifests per split, evaluating every candidate on common calibration samples will raise pairwise rerun agreement of the selected configuration by at least 15 percentage points and reduce independent-test ECE regret relative to the population-best grid point by at least 0.005 compared with assigning independent calibration samples to every candidate.

Across 60 deterministic splits with 16 calibration seeds of n=75 and a locked 21-by-21 affine-logit grid, adding the preregistered selection penalty 0.002*((a-1)^2+b^2) to mean ECE will reduce boundary-parameter selections by at least 50% and improve the independently evaluated mean paired ECE reduction by at least 0.01 relative to unpenalized selection.

Across 80 deterministic splits from a perfectly calibrated null DGP with q=P(Y=1|X), selecting from a locked 21-by-21 affine-logit grid using mean 15-bin ECE over exactly 16 seeds of n=50 will show an apparent reused-sample paired ECE reduction of at least 0.08 on average, while independent n=10000 evaluation will show a mean paired reduction no greater than 0 and will favor the identity calibrator.

For a preregistered finite archive language containing at most three canonically ordered entries, six legal path names, and policies over three Boolean variables, exhaustive enumeration of every normalized archive model will produce canonical bytes that two independently written parsers both accept and map back to the original model in 100% of cases; exhaustive enumeration of all byte strings admitted by either parser within the resulting maximum length will reveal no additional accepted canonical archive.

For 128 policy mutants that each differ from a reference policy on exactly one of the 256 assignments of eight Boolean variables, an independently implemented exhaustive truth-table equivalence oracle will detect all 128 mutants, whereas suites of 16 uniformly sampled assignments will miss at least 85% of them on average across 100 deterministic seeds.

Among 30 seeded lossy canonicalizer mutants that delete, merge, truncate, or default a policy field while remaining deterministic, idempotent, and accepted by an independent parser, all 30 will pass structural acceptance and fixed-point checks, but exact finite-domain policy-equivalence checking will reject at least 27.

For 24 serializer mutants that preserve the normalized policy model but independently violate one canonical byte rule involving field order, integer encoding, redundant defaults, string escaping, duplicate representation, or archive-entry order, exhaustive policy-behavior comparison will classify all 24 outputs as equivalent to the reference, while an independent canonical-form verifier will reject all 24.

Against 40 single-edit parser mutants covering length bounds, shortest-form integers, duplicate fields, ordering, UTF-8 validity, trailing bytes, and nesting depth, a 400-case suite generated solely from the published grammar and boundary contracts will kill at least 90% of mutants, while an equal-sized uniformly random byte suite using the same acceptance-disagreement oracle will kill no more than 60%.

For 30 canonicalizer mutants involving omitted sorting, unstable duplicate handling, incomplete normalization, retained defaults, and nonminimal encodings, a suite built from 200 independently generated semantic models and their permutations, redundant-field variants, and equivalent encodings will kill at least 24 mutants, whereas testing the same mutants only on the 200 already-canonical reference outputs for acceptance and idempotence will kill no more than 10.

Across 45 seeded single-stage mutants divided equally among parsing, canonicalization, and policy evaluation, the ordered disagreement signature consisting of accepted language, normalized model, canonical bytes, and complete policy truth table will correctly identify the mutated stage for at least 42 mutants; a diagnosis using only final pass/fail and policy decisions will correctly identify no more than 30.

For 24 normalization-rule mutants affecting Unicode normalization, case folding, path separators, default elision, and numeric minimality, a generator and verifier that reuse the mutant canonicalizer's normalization helper will report agreement on all of their self-generated archives, whereas a generator derived from declarative rule tables and a separately coded verifier will reject or byte-disagree with at least 22 mutants while accepting all 24 unmutated controls.

For a deterministic corpus of 128 baselines and 3,840 case–mutant pairs, a strict schema-plus-cross-record validator will accept all 3,968 complete records and reject all 320 seeded audit defects, comprising 40 instances each of a missing required field, missing payload/hash partner, duplicate unit identifier, orphan artifact reference, baseline–pair mismatch, invalid outcome enumeration, inconsistent aggregate count, and digest/length mismatch.

Two independently implemented canonical JSON serializers following one frozen rule set for key ordering, Unicode handling, integer formatting, binary encoding, and absent versus null fields will produce byte-identical records and SHA-256 digests for all 3,968 units under 100 randomized in-memory key-order permutations per unit; ordinary noncanonical JSON serialization will produce at least two distinct digests for at least 95% of units.

Across 32 synthetic state-sensitive mutant fixtures involving global counters, random-generator carryover, parser caches, environment mutation, working-directory changes, and retained temporary files, two executions launched in separately sanitized fresh processes will yield identical payloads and hashes for all 32 fixtures, whereas two executions in one reused worker process will disagree on at least one parser, fixed-point, semantic, distance, or counterexample field for at least 24 fixtures.

An independently coded, execution-disabled auditor given the full semantic-bitset and counterexample payloads plus their hashes will recompute every behavioral distance and verify every classification and first-counterexample claim for all 3,840 pairs, while the same auditor given a variant retaining only hashes of those payloads will be able to recompute zero behavioral distances and verify no counterexample contents, despite successfully checking all supplied artifact digests.

For 512 deterministically generated semantic bitsets of lengths 1 through 257, two independent implementations using an explicit framing format containing domain identifier, bit count, byte count, and least-significant-bit-first packing will agree on every stable hash; if bit order and terminal padding rules are omitted, independently reasonable MSB-first and LSB-first encoders will disagree on at least 450 of the 512 hashes while decoding to differently indexed observations.

For 64 non-equivalent pairs each having at least four counterexample assignments or schedules, recording the minimum witness under a frozen total order will yield the identical first-counterexample payload and hash across 100 deterministic permutations of exploration order for every pair; recording the first witness encountered will yield at least two distinct counterexample hashes for at least 48 pairs.

In 128 seeded provenance attacks that swap valid same-type artifact references between case–mutant pairs while leaving each artifact and its ordinary payload hash unchanged, payload-hash verification alone will accept all 128 altered bundles, whereas a context-bound digest over unit identifier, stage name, ordered parent digests, payload digest, and schema version will reject all 128 and accept every unmodified bundle.

On the complete 128-baseline and 3,840-pair bundle, content-addressed storage that writes each distinct source archive, output archive, semantic payload, and counterexample once will reconstruct every record with identical artifact hashes while reducing total artifact bytes by at least 60% relative to embedding all referenced payloads separately in each pair record; full validation and reconstruction will complete in under five minutes on a laptop.

For 96 pairs of validly signed release manifests that contain the same literal Merkle root but differ in exactly one of inventory identifier, scope, canonicalization-specification digest, tree type, record count, or proof-service identifier, a transparency entry containing only the root will authenticate both manifests, whereas an entry containing the digest of the complete signed manifest will accept the intended manifest and reject the alternate in all 96 pairs.

Across 120 deterministic metadata mix-and-match attacks combining individually valid timestamp, snapshot, and root-bearing release objects from different publication generations, a TUF-style metadata graph that binds every child version and digest will reject all 120 attacks and accept all 40 coherent controls, while a verifier that checks each object's signature independently without parent-to-child bindings will accept at least 90 attacks.

After observing release version v, a verifier that persistently records the highest accepted version and its manifest digest will reject all 100 replay attempts presenting a still-unexpired release with version less than v or a different digest at version v, whereas a stateless verifier checking only signatures and expiration will accept all 100; both verifiers will accept every one of 50 strictly advancing control sequences.

In 100 forged-root releases produced using one compromised key from a three-key release role, a 2-of-3 threshold verifier will reject every forgery while accepting all 100 legitimate releases signed by any authorized pair; a single-signature configuration using the compromised key will accept every forgery, and the threshold format will add no more than 256 serialized signature bytes per release.

Across 80 deterministic key-transition sequences comprising 40 legitimate rotations and 40 attacker substitutions, a rollover protocol requiring each new trust-root object to satisfy both the previous threshold and the newly declared threshold will accept all legitimate rotations and reject all substitutions; static key pinning will reject all 40 legitimate rotations, while trust-on-first-use of the latest advertised key will accept all 40 substitutions.

For 64 simulated split-view attacks in which a transparency service signs two checkpoints of the same tree size with different roots and supplies a valid inclusion proof within each fork, isolated inclusion-only verifiers will accept both views, whereas verifiers that exchange their latest checkpoints once and require equal-size checkpoints to have identical roots will detect all 64 forks; neither method will flag any of 64 consistent-log controls.

In an exhaustive crash-state model with durable publication of records, proofs, a signed root manifest, and a signed latest-release pointer, enforcing the dependency order records-before-proofs-before-manifest-before-latest will yield zero reachable states in which an authenticated latest pointer names an unavailable dependency; allowing the four publication events in arbitrary order will expose such a broken authenticated latest state in at least 18 of the 24 event orderings.

During a simulated transparency-service outage, a verifier using a previously witnessed signed checkpoint plus content-addressed copies of the included manifest and proofs will accept all 80 requests whose checkpoint age is within a configured 24-hour bound and reject all 40 requests whose checkpoint is older than that bound; a verifier requiring live log access will reject all 120 requests, while a permissive offline verifier without the age bound will incorrectly accept all 40 stale cases.

Across 96 output-swap mutants in which the attacker replaces a stage output and recomputes every affected payload hash, context field, descendant reference, and signature under an attacker-controlled key, a verifier anchored to the original authenticated root will reject all 96, whereas the same verification logic starting from the attacker-supplied unauthenticated root will accept all 96; both conditions will accept all 32 unmodified controls.

For 80 paired source-and-output swaps that import a valid source-output pair from another unit while leaving the global artifact inventory unchanged and preserving successful transformation re-execution, an authenticated root committing only to the unordered artifact inventory will accept all 80 altered graphs, whereas an authenticated root also committing to canonical tuples of unit, operation, source edge, and output edge will reject all 80 and accept all 40 unmodified controls.

Across 90 source-only swaps constructed from non-injective transformations such as case folding, comment removal, record sorting, and whitespace normalization, re-execution plus output-hash comparison will accept all 90 because the substituted source produces the original output, while a verifier enforcing an authenticated unit-to-authorized-source mapping will reject all 90 and accept all 30 authorized alternative-source controls.

For 96 cross-stage swaps between records having compatible schemas and byte-identical input and output types, a verifier checking only DAG well-formedness, artifact hashes, and membership of the signer in a global trusted-key set will accept all 96, whereas a verifier enforcing authenticated stage-specific signer capabilities and an allowed stage-transition matrix will reject all 96; both verifiers will accept all 32 correctly placed controls.

In a corpus containing 48 order-sensitive multi-parent operations and 48 operations explicitly declared parent-order invariant, reversing each parent list will be accepted in all 96 cases by a verifier that unconditionally sorts parents before hashing, while a declaration-aware verifier will reject all 48 order-sensitive reversals, accept all 48 order-invariant reversals with unchanged semantic identity, and accept all 32 unmodified controls.

Across 96 adaptive schema mutants comprising 48 substitutions of a structurally permissive schema under an existing schema identifier and 48 downgrades to an older schema that omits source, stage, or parent-binding requirements, a name-based resolver with no authenticated version floor will parse and accept all 96, whereas a verifier whose authenticated root binds the schema-document digest and minimum permitted version will reject all 96 and accept all 32 records using authorized schema versions.

For 120 provenance-reference mutants using dot segments, repeated separators, percent-encoding, Unicode normalization variants, case variants, and platform-specific separator aliases that all resolve to an existing artifact, a verifier comparing only the resolved target's content hash will accept all 120, whereas a verifier requiring the reference spelling to equal a root-bound canonical logical path and rejecting non-unique canonical keys will reject all 120; both will accept all 40 canonical-path controls.

For 80 complete-manifest replacements whose manifests are internally consistent and signed by keys valid for a different synthetic project namespace, a verifier beginning from a pinned authenticated delegation root and enforcing namespace- and role-scoped signing authority will reject all 80, while the same verifier beginning from each replacement's self-supplied unauthenticated delegation root will accept all 80; both modes will accept all 40 replacements authorized by the pinned project's delegation policy.
